default.summary: llm-d-router's built-in config, used when a run names none: queue depth, KV cache and prefix scorers, then the highest score.
default.yaml:
apiVersion: llm-d.ai/v1
kind: EndpointPickerConfig
plugins:
- type: queue-scorer
- type: kv-cache-utilization-scorer
- type: prefix-cache-scorer
- type: metrics-data-source
- type: core-metrics-extractor
schedulingProfiles:
- name: default
  plugins:
  - pluginRef: queue-scorer
    weight: 2
  - pluginRef: kv-cache-utilization-scorer
    weight: 2
  - pluginRef: prefix-cache-scorer
    weight: 3

pd-always.summary: Disaggregated: every request prefills on the prefill pool, then decodes on the decode pool.
pd-always.yaml:
apiVersion: llm-d.ai/v1
kind: EndpointPickerConfig
plugins:
- type: approx-prefix-cache-producer
  parameters:
    maxPrefixTokensToMatch: 16384
    lruCapacityPerServer: 31250
- type: prefix-cache-scorer
- type: queue-scorer
- type: prefill-filter
- type: decode-filter
- type: max-score-picker
- type: always-disagg-pd-decider
- type: disagg-profile-handler
  parameters:
    deciders:
      prefill: always-disagg-pd-decider
schedulingProfiles:
- name: prefill
  plugins:
  - pluginRef: prefill-filter
  - pluginRef: max-score-picker
  - pluginRef: prefix-cache-scorer
    weight: 2
  - pluginRef: queue-scorer
    weight: 1
- name: decode
  plugins:
  - pluginRef: decode-filter
  - pluginRef: max-score-picker
  - pluginRef: prefix-cache-scorer
    weight: 2
  - pluginRef: queue-scorer
    weight: 1

prefix-affinity.summary: Keeps requests that share a prefix on the instance that served it first.
prefix-affinity.yaml:
apiVersion: llm-d.ai/v1
kind: EndpointPickerConfig
plugins:
- type: approx-prefix-cache-producer
- type: prefix-cache-scorer
- type: max-score-picker
- type: single-profile-handler
schedulingProfiles:
- name: default
  plugins:
  - pluginRef: prefix-cache-scorer
  - pluginRef: max-score-picker

queue.summary: Sends each request to the instance with the shortest queue.
queue.yaml:
apiVersion: llm-d.ai/v1
kind: EndpointPickerConfig
plugins:
- type: queue-scorer
- type: max-score-picker
- type: single-profile-handler
schedulingProfiles:
- name: default
  plugins:
  - pluginRef: queue-scorer
  - pluginRef: max-score-picker

random.summary: Spreads requests at random; the baseline every scorer has to beat.
random.yaml:
apiVersion: llm-d.ai/v1
kind: EndpointPickerConfig
plugins:
- type: random-picker
- type: single-profile-handler
schedulingProfiles:
- name: default
  plugins:
  - pluginRef: random-picker

setup.script:
# the stack that priced this report (needs git and Go)
git clone --branch v0.17.1 --depth 1 https://github.com/inference-sim/inference-sim.git inference-sim && \
  (cd inference-sim && go build -o blis main.go) && \
  export PATH="$PWD/inference-sim:$PATH"

git clone --branch v0.14.1 --depth 1 https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-substrate.git blis-substrate && \
  export SUBSTRATE_CATALOG="$PWD/blis-substrate/catalog" && \
  export SUBSTRATE_REGISTRY="$PWD/blis-substrate/registry"

# the commands run from this repo: router configs live here, scenarios/ is where you save each scenario
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-config-search.git && cd blis-config-search && mkdir -p scenarios

# the replay corpus (not vendored anywhere; checked against its digest)
mkdir -p .corpus
# fetch the corpus to .corpus/traces.jsonl (see SETUP.md)
echo "29b6a19e751ff5230771519aab755f80a0f43a4ba9cf96b72d3a6a437ec99276  .corpus/traces.jsonl" | shasum -a 256 -c
setup.sweep:
# in the blis-config-search checkout, after the install script
python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install pyyaml
python3 -I scripts/run_experiment.py reports/muse-spark-open-816b-a42b-h100-agentx-8node/spec.yaml --dry-run --catalog "$SUBSTRATE_CATALOG"
python3 -I scripts/run_experiment.py reports/muse-spark-open-816b-a42b-h100-agentx-8node/spec.yaml \
  --blis "$(command -v blis)" --catalog "$SUBSTRATE_CATALOG" --registry "$SUBSTRATE_REGISTRY" \
  --out repro/

spec_yaml:
name: muse-spark-open-816b-a42b-h100-agentx-8node
scenario:
  model: muse-spark-open-816b-a42b-nvfp4
  hardware: h100
  workload_spec: workloads/agentx-run-recipe.yaml
  gpus: 64
  cluster:
    fabric: roce-200g
    gpus_per_node: 8
  engine:
    max_model_len: 262144
    gpu_memory_utilization: 0.95
  concurrency:
  - 64
  - 128
  - 256
  - 512
  replay:
    corpus: .corpus/traces.jsonl
    corpus_cache: /tmp/agx-cache-muse-h100-8node
sweeps:
- name: topology
  narrative: Eight single-node TP8 instances are the control every other sweep is
    read against.
  num-instances:
  - 8
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 8
    dp:
    - 1
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
- name: ep-off
  narrative: Replicating all 256 experts instead of sharding them should cost KV room
    and throughput against the EP twins in topology.
  num-instances:
  - 8
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 8
    dp:
    - 1
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - false
- name: pipeline
  narrative: Pipeline stages should trail data-parallel shapes of the same width,
    since each stage adds a boundary hop per decode step.
  num-instances:
  - 4
  - 2
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 8
    - 4
    pp:
    - 2
    - 4
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
- name: moe-collective
  narrative: At in-node EP width 8 on NVLink the all-to-all backend should matter
    little.
  num-instances:
  - 8
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 8
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
  engine:
    all2all_backend:
    - deepep_high_throughput
    - deepep_low_latency
    - deepep_v2
    - pplx
- name: kv-capacity
  narrative: fp8 KV should matter most on 8x TP8, whose 80 GiB ranks leave the least
    KV room (fp8 was +40% there at c=32 in the 8gpu report).
  num-instances:
  - 8
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 8
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
  engine:
    cache_dtype:
    - auto
    - fp8
- name: batch-caps
  narrative: A seq cap of 32 should bind on 8x TP8 at 512 lanes.
  num-instances:
  - 8
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 8
    dp:
    - 1
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
  engine:
    max_num_seqs:
    - 32
    - 256
    max_num_batched_tokens:
    - 4096
    - 16384
- name: routing-prefix-cache
  narrative: prefix-affinity should only beat queue and random with caching on, and
    eight instances give it the most room to win.
  num-instances:
  - 8
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 8
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
  engine:
    enable_prefix_caching:
    - true
    - false
  router:
    endpoint_picker_config:
    - random.yaml
    - queue.yaml
    - prefix-affinity.yaml
- name: prefill-chunking
  narrative: Capping long prefills should trade a little peak throughput for a much
    lower ITL p99 at saturation.
  num-instances:
  - 8
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 8
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
  engine:
    long_prefill_token_threshold:
    - 2048
- name: pd-ratio
  narrative: Decode-heavy ratios should win on AgentX, since cached prefixes leave
    only a short uncached tail to prefill per turn -- and the RoCE handoff taxes the
    prefill-heavy splits more.
  prefill-instances:
  - 1
  - 2
  - 3
  - 4
  decode-instances:
  - 7
  - 6
  - 5
  - 4
  prefill:
    parallel:
      tp:
      - 8
      enable_expert_parallel:
      - true
  decode:
    parallel:
      tp:
      - 8
      enable_expert_parallel:
      - true
  router:
    endpoint_picker_config:
    - pd-prefix-based.yaml
    plugins:
      prefix-based-pd-decider:
        parameters:
          nonCachedTokens:
          - 256
          - 1024
          - 4096
          - 16384
- name: pd-always
  narrative: Splitting every request should trail the threshold arms, because a turn
    with a cached prefix pays a cross-node RoCE handoff for little prefill.
  prefill-instances:
  - 1
  - 2
  - 3
  - 4
  decode-instances:
  - 7
  - 6
  - 5
  - 4
  prefill:
    parallel:
      tp:
      - 8
      enable_expert_parallel:
      - true
  decode:
    parallel:
      tp:
      - 8
      enable_expert_parallel:
      - true
  router:
    endpoint_picker_config:
    - pd-always.yaml
- name: pd-wide-decode
  narrative: TP16 decode instances should hold ITL at higher load than TP8 ones, trading
    batch slots for faster steps.
  prefill-instances:
  - 2
  - 4
  - 6
  decode-instances:
  - 3
  - 2
  - 1
  prefill:
    parallel:
      tp:
      - 8
      enable_expert_parallel:
      - true
  decode:
    parallel:
      tp:
      - 16
      enable_expert_parallel:
      - true
  router:
    endpoint_picker_config:
    - pd-prefix-based.yaml
    plugins:
      prefix-based-pd-decider:
        parameters:
          nonCachedTokens:
          - 256
          - 4096
- name: pd-pool-engine
  narrative: A bigger prefill budget should matter on the prefill-light layout and
    a decode-pool prefill cap on the decode-heavy one.
  prefill-instances:
  - 2
  - 4
  decode-instances:
  - 6
  - 4
  prefill:
    parallel:
      tp:
      - 8
      enable_expert_parallel:
      - true
    engine:
      max_num_batched_tokens:
      - 8192
      - 16384
  decode:
    parallel:
      tp:
      - 8
      enable_expert_parallel:
      - true
    engine:
      long_prefill_token_threshold:
      - 0
      - 2048
  router:
    endpoint_picker_config:
    - pd-prefix-based.yaml
- name: pd-decode-cudagraph
  narrative: Full graph capture on the decode pool should lower ITL by a few percent,
    with FULL_DECODE_ONLY matching FULL there.
  prefill-instances:
  - 3
  decode-instances:
  - 5
  prefill:
    parallel:
      tp:
      - 8
      enable_expert_parallel:
      - true
  decode:
    parallel:
      tp:
      - 8
      enable_expert_parallel:
      - true
    engine:
      cudagraph_mode:
      - FULL
      - FULL_DECODE_ONLY
  router:
    endpoint_picker_config:
    - pd-prefix-based.yaml
- name: cudagraph
  narrative: FULL capture should beat the PIECEWISE default by a few percent, and
    NONE should collapse.
  num-instances:
  - 8
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 8
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
  engine:
    cudagraph_mode:
    - NONE
    - FULL
